comments.body:
## /rebar-debug Phase 1 — confirmed mechanisms + NOT-A-BUG classification (no code change)

Investigation complete. Two mechanisms proven; **both classify as not-a-bug**, so the Phase 2
auto-fix guard held and no code was written. Evidence below; the disposition is the user's call.

### AC #1 — ANSWERED: `rebar create` does NOT consult the overlap detector

`create_core` — `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:113-281` — is the single seam every create
funnels through (CLI `composer.py:344,440`; library `_lib_writes.py:120,159`; MCP
`_mcp_writes.py:150`; `idea()` `_lib_writes.py:184`). Its complete check list:

| line | check |
|---|---|
| 158 | `validate_creation_channel` |
| 162-168 | ticket_type enum |
| 169-172 | title non-empty, <=255 |
| 174-176 | priority 0-4 |
| 180-181 | `.env-id` init gate |
| 184-199 | parent exists / has CREATE-or-SNAPSHOT / not closed |
| **263** | `append_event(... "CREATE" ...)` — the emit |
| 270-275 | post-emit advisory `description_cap_warning` (never blocks) |

No import of `rebar.llm.overlap`, no `search_states`, no similarity call. The only cross-ticket
read is the single parent lookup at `:194`.

**Runtime proof** (isolated store, `/tmp/dupetest`): three tickets created with the byte-identical
title `"Canonical work item"` -> `403b-74ed`, `c6ea-0f44`, `f8ca-a960`. Zero duplicate signal on
any of them; the only stderr was the unrelated `file_impact` nudge.

### MEASURED DUPLICATE RATE (method + sample size)

Sample: **all 2679 tickets** (`rebar list --include-archived -o json`). Ground truth: the **43
recorded `duplicates` links**, closed transitively into clusters -> **51 duplicate pairs** (~2% of
the store). Manually added one unrecorded pair (`039b-d179`/`baeb-4f4b`, case 2 — unrecorded
precisely because of mechanism B).

**Exact normalized-title match (case/punctuation/whitespace folded):**

- **RECALL 14% (7/51).** 44 of 51 real duplicates are semantic, not lexical, e.g.
  `"Sweep walks full git history per ticket under the store lock"` vs `"Out-of-band compaction
  sweep holds the shared store write lock for many minutes"`. Title match cannot see these.
- **PRECISION 18%** unqualified (7 true / 38 pairs). The FP mass is two legitimate classes:
  automated recurring filings (`[binding-drift] bridge-fsck found 1 unhealed binding drift(s)`,
  6 tickets over 27 days — genuinely distinct occurrences) and test/probe fixtures
  (`repro race target` x6, `unknown-option probe` x4, `EXPERIMENT (delete me)` x3).
- **Constrained to a <5 min creation window and excluding fixture titles: precision 100% (7/7).**

**The temporal finding that reframes the ticket.** Every same-title true duplicate was created
within **171 seconds** of its twin (deltas: 8.9s, 10.9s, 18.7s, 19.5s, 28.4s, 45s, 171s). Across
all 51 pairs the distribution is bimodal — 6 under a minute, 13 over a day, median 6 hours.

So the same-title cases are **not** search-first failures. At the instant agent A ran its
pre-create `search`, ticket B did not yet exist. AGENTS.md's search-first instruction is not the
control that failed here; it could not have applied.

**Store visibility (git ancestry of the CREATE commits):** 6 of the 7 same-title pairs were
created in a strictly **linear** tickets-branch lineage 1-4 commits apart — the earlier ticket was
fully present in the local store when the later one was created (e.g. `5a90-ec98`'s CREATE commit
`1386ba1b14` has `ea16-dd54`'s CREATE `e1e4d0c07b` as its **direct parent**, 10.9s apart). Only
`788b-a5dd`/`4f50-b1f2` was divergent. So create-time detection is *technically feasible* — it
would have caught 6 of 7 same-title dupes (= 12% of all known duplicates).

### MECHANISM A — no create-time detection. Classification: **feature-request**

Cited design authority: **ADR 0086** (`docs/adr/0086-cross-ticket-overlap.md`, Accepted
2026-07-09) deliberately placed detection elsewhere:

> "Add a store-wide, advisory-only overlap detector that runs **during the plan-review invocation
> window (before claim)**" ... "**overlap runs at review time**"

and chose digest-BM25F specifically because enrichment "must run **async off the hot write
path**". The detector is **enabled in this project** (`verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets = True`,
verified by resolving `rebar.config.compose_config('.')`) and runs where designed
(`plan_review/__init__.py:771-779`). It does not title-match by design — its BM25F fields are
`problem_keywords`/`component_or_area`/`key_entities`/`propositions` (`overlap/retrieve.py:26-31`);
title is not a field.

So create-time title surfacing was never designed, never approved, and the design authority
affirmatively chose a different placement with stated reasons. That is a scope extension, not a
defect.

**Cost, measured — why this is not a cheap add.** There is **no title index anywhere** in
`src/rebar` (grep for `title_index|by_title|title_cache|normalize_title`: zero hits). Materializing
titles costs:

| approach | measured |
|---|---|
| `rebar.list_tickets()` | **2.1 s**, uncached (repeats at 2.09-2.23 s) |
| full SNAPSHOT read (4894 files) | **~850 ms** warm |
| `rebar search` (`reduce_all_tickets`, no index) | O(N tickets x E events); 2.7 s wall |
| the comparison itself, once titles are in hand | **12 ms** |

The cost is entirely in materializing the corpus. Putting any of these on the synchronous create
path reintroduces exactly the `moist-short-lionfish` (`958e-f4b3-275c-4154`) regression that
`a02eedbb6e` just fixed — that was 486 ms/write against a declared 20 ms budget, degrading 6.3x at
16 concurrent walkers. Avoiding it requires a **new persistent title index** with its own
invariants (rotation, concurrent writers, torn-read safety, cache invalidation) — the shape of
`queue.py:295-335`, i.e. an architectural addition, not a bug fix.

**Verdict: a create-time title guard does not clear the bar.** 14% recall, bought with a new
write-path index in the precise regression class just remediated. The 100%-precision variant
(same title + <5 min) is the interesting design if this is ever pursued, because the burst
signature both discriminates cleanly *and* bounds the scan — but that is a design proposal
needing approval, not a defect repair.

### MECHANISM B — `link <closed-source> ... duplicates` refused. Classification: **intended-behavior** (sanctioned alternative exists and works)

Guard: `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:284-290`, relation-agnostic:

```
cannot create duplicates link - source ticket 'f8ca-a960-93dd-48ec' is closed.
Reopen it first with: ticket transition f8ca-a960-93dd-48ec closed open
```

**Runtime-proven both ways** in the isolated store. The refusal reproduces exactly as reported.
But the remedy the error itself names **works end-to-end**:

```
rebar reopen f8ca-a960     -> reopened: closed -> open
rebar link f8ca-a960 403b-74ed duplicates -> linked (duplicates)
rebar transition f8ca-a960 open closed --class duplicate -> transitioned
final: status=closed  deps=[('duplicates','403b-74ed-f6c7-459d')]
```

The ticket ends **closed with a machine-readable `duplicates` link** — exactly the outcome AC #4
asks for. AC #4's own wording accepts this: *"or a sanctioned alternative exists for recording a
duplicate relation after the source is closed."* It exists, it is named in the error text, and it
is verified working. The re-close is exempt from completion verification via the
`_administrative_disposition` short-circuit (`close_precheck.py:598-600`), so it is not a heavy path.

Case (2)'s agent left the relation in a prose comment rather than following the two-command remedy
the error printed. That is an agent-behaviour gap, not a tool defect.

### Attribution

Per the not-a-bug guard there is **no defect to attribute**, so no `caused_by` is recorded.
Recording the searches for the record:

- `git blame -w -C -M -L 280,298 src/rebar/graph/_links.py` -> all lines `b534f47a7f9`
  (2026-06-08, *"Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler into standalone rebar"*) — the
  repo-genesis import, i.e. a **carrier**; the guard is pre-history for this repo.
- `git log -S 'source ticket' -- .../graph/_links.py` -> same single commit; no later change
  altered the behaviour. **Date test: the guard predates by ~2 months the commit that made
  `duplicates` links load-bearing** (`94df7a8db5a`, 2026-08-12, *"Tell a duplicate close it needs
  a link"*, `rebar-ticket: c8fd-1274-bcea-408e`) — so nothing regressed; the behaviour has been
  constant since genesis.
- Mechanism A is an **omission by design choice**, not by miss: ADR 0086 scoped detection to
  review time. The ticket that "should have covered" create-time detection does not exist because
  the capability was never scoped.

### Recommended disposition (user's call)

1. **Mechanism B / AC #4** — no code change. If the two named tickets should carry real links,
   the runnable path is `reopen -> link ... duplicates -> transition ... --class duplicate` on
   `elfish-saltwater-pika` (`ea16-dd54`) and `decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` (`baeb-4f4b`). That is
   a status mutation on tickets outside this debug's scope, so **I have not done it** — it needs
   an explicit go-ahead.
2. **Mechanism A / AC #2-3** — if create-time surfacing is still wanted, it should be filed as a
   design ticket against ADR 0086 (an ADR amendment), specified as *same normalized title +
   bounded recency window + advisory-only*, patterned on `description_cap_warning`
   (`composer.py:270-275`) for the non-blocking surface and on the lionfish gate marker
   (`queue.py:295-335`) for the O(1) read. Expected yield, measured: ~12% of duplicates.
3. A cheaper control targeting the *actual* signature (bursts, same clone, ~10s apart) may be
   worth more than title matching: these look like double-submits/retries, so an idempotency or
   confirm-on-recent-identical-create affordance would address the observed cases more directly.

comments.body:
## Session handoff — investigation concluded NOT-A-BUG; the ticket needs a disposition close

State at handoff: `in_progress`, zero merged commits, no attestation. The Phase 1 comment above
records a completed `/rebar-debug` investigation: **two mechanisms proven, both classified
not-a-bug, no code change proposed.**

**Why I did not close it:** a not-a-bug disposition is a judgment about intended behaviour, and
this session did not run the investigation. Closing someone else's analysis on its summary line —
without reading the mechanisms and agreeing with the classification — would be exactly the
rubber-stamp the classification exists to prevent. The five ACs are also unticked and, if the
not-a-bug finding stands, most are moot rather than met, which is a distinction that belongs in
the close record.

**What the next session should do:** read the Phase 1 comment, decide whether you agree with both
classifications, and then either

- close it as a disposition — `rebar transition exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish in_progress closed
  --class=not_a_bug` — recording in a comment that the ACs are **moot rather than satisfied**, and
  why; or
- if you disagree with the classification, say so with evidence and re-scope the ticket.

Do not leave it `in_progress` indefinitely: a proven not-a-bug that stays open reads to `ready`
and `next-batch` as available work and will be re-investigated by someone else. This session saw
that exact waste — a flaky test that two independent sessions had hit and neither recorded as a
work item, so it kept being rediscovered.

If the classification stands, consider whether the underlying observation (duplicate tickets only
surfacing after an agent is mid-implementation) deserves a separate ticket for the *workflow* gap
even though the *mechanism* is working as designed. That is a different claim from the one
investigated here.

## Operator ruling (2026-08-21): reclassify as enhancement (bug -> task), return to open

The operator approved reclassifying this ticket as an **enhancement**, per the /rebar-debug Phase-1 finding recorded above: `create_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`) — the single seam every create funnels through (CLI, library, MCP, `idea()`) — performs NO duplicate/similarity check BY DESIGN; its complete validation list is channel, type enum, title length, priority, and store init. Absent duplicate detection at create time is therefore intended current behaviour, not a violated contract, and adding same-title/similarity flagging at creation is new capability — task-shaped design work wanting a plan and review.

The observed cost (two full agent dispatches spent discovering duplication mid-implementation) stands as the motivation; the evidence and ACs are unchanged. Type changed bug -> task ("enhancement" is not a rebar ticket type; task is the supported form) and status returned in_progress -> open so it can be planned and claimed as designed work rather than sitting claimed with no active session.

## Implemented, merged, and closed — evidence

**Design chosen (per operator ruling + OSS grounding).** Create-time, advisory-only,
same-normalized-title duplicate surfacing — the shape GitHub/GitLab (filing-time similar-issue
surfacing) and Kubernetes / VS Code triage bots (flag immediately after creation, never block)
use. Implemented as a bounded O(window) probe, not an O(store) scan: a rolling
`recent-creates.json` sidecar journal (600 s window, ~3.5x the 171 s max observed true-duplicate
delta) probed inside `create_core` under a dedicated `fcntl.flock` (the `_hlc_lock` pattern), so
concurrent creates serialize and the later observes the earlier. Gated on the existing
`verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` key. Operation-linked/in-process (CLI, library, MCP, `idea()`
all funnel through `create_core`) — no CI dependency.

**AC #1 (recorded).** `rebar create` does NOT consult the overlap detector: before this change
`create_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:113-281`) performed only channel/type/title/
priority/init/parent checks — no `rebar.llm.overlap` import (confirmed by the Phase-1
investigation and re-verified this session). The create-time probe now lives at
`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` -> `rebar._commands.recent_creates.duplicate_create_warning`,
called immediately after `append_event`.

**AC #2/#3 (surfaced, non-blocking).** RED-first evidence: the new test
`tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py` failed with `KeyError: 'duplicate_warning'`
before the implementation, then all 12 tests passed after — covering: same-title warns with
candidate id + status on library/CLI(`create` + `idea`)/MCP surfaces; distinct titles silent;
case/punctuation/whitespace normalization; stale-window silence; flag-off = silent + zero
journal footprint; corrupt journal never disturbs the write; warned create still succeeds
(exit 0); two concurrent same-title creates serialize so one observes the other.

**AC #4 (duplicates links).** Sanctioned alternative executed:
- `elfish-saltwater-pika` already carried `duplicates -> 5a90-ec98-af5a-48d0` (recorded earlier).
- `decagonal-indisposed-tamarin`: reopen -> `link baeb-4f4b-3227-457e 039b-d179-b669-4439
  duplicates` -> re-close `--class duplicate` executed this session; the ticket now ends closed
  WITH the machine-readable link.

**AC #5 (gates).** `make lint` PASS, `make typecheck` PASS (640 files),
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check`: active=43 new=0 increased=0 (stale=6 pre-existing).

**Landed.** Gerrit change 2147, LLM-Review +1 (rebar review bot), Verified +1 (rebar CI bot),
0 unresolved comments; submitted; merged into main as `55020dff94cca12410cac17cc258d4447d9af828`
("Warn about same-title duplicates at create").

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
Duplicate tickets are filed for work that already exists and only discovered
mid-implementation. Twice in one session (2026-08-19/20) a duplicate carried the SAME TITLE
as its twin and passed creation unflagged: `elfish-saltwater-pika` (ea16-dd54) and
`decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` (baeb-4f4b). The /rebar-debug Phase-1 investigation (first
comment) measured the store: every same-title true duplicate was created within 171 s of its
twin, and "same normalized title + <5 min window" scored 100% precision (7/7) on the full
2679-ticket store. The operator ruling (2026-08-21 comment) reclassified this bug -> task:
absent create-time detection is intended current behaviour (ADR 0086 placed the heavy
overlap detector at review time, off the hot write path), so this is designed new capability.

## Design — create-time advisory same-title duplicate warning (bounded, O(1))
Matches mainstream OSS trackers (GitHub/GitLab surface similar issues at filing time;
Kubernetes/VS Code triage bots flag likely duplicates immediately after creation):
detection at CREATE, advisory-only (never blocks), reusing cheap existing signals.

**Mechanism.** A small rolling "recent creates" journal — a store-wide sidecar
(`StorePaths(tracker).sidecar("recent-creates.json")`, the canonical-store keying the overlap
enrich gate marker uses, bug da68-fc7c) — records `{ts_ns, id, alias, title, title_norm}` for
each create, pruned to a fixed recency window (600 s, ~3.5x the largest observed
true-duplicate delta of 171 s). On every create, `create_core` probes the journal for a
normalized-title match (case/punctuation/whitespace folded) BEFORE appending its own entry,
then rewrites the journal atomically (same-dir temp file + `os.replace`).
**Concurrency: the whole read-prune-probe-append-rewrite is one critical section under a
dedicated exclusive `fcntl.flock` on the sidecar `recent-creates.lock`** — the `_hlc_lock`
pattern proven for the HLC sidecar RMW (`src/rebar/_store/hlc.py`): held only for the one
small-file RMW, never nested with the store write lock (no ordering hazard), and dropped by
the kernel if the holder dies. Two near-simultaneous creates therefore serialize: the
second's probe observes the first's entry (the burst case the feature targets) and no
rewrite clobbers a just-appended row. Cost is one flock + one small-file read + one write —
O(window), never O(store); no title index, no store scan, honouring the moist-short-lionfish
write-path budget lesson (bug 6148 class). On a match, the single candidate ticket is
reduced (one-ticket `reduce_ticket`, O(1)) to report its LIVE status in the message.

**Gating.** The probe runs only when `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is true — the
existing advisory duplicate-detection key (on for this project); no new config surface.
Flag off = no journal, no probe, zero write-path footprint.

**Surfacing (the description_cap_warning pattern, ticket 594b).** `create_core` returns a
new `duplicate_warning` key; each surface emits it on its own channel after the write
commits: CLI stderr via `_warn_stderr` in BOTH CLI creates — `create_cli` (`composer.py`)
and `idea_cli` (`src/rebar/_commands/idea.py`, which calls `create_core` directly) —
keeping stdout pure in both output modes; library logger + `duplicate_warning` in the
`return_alias=True` dict (`create_ticket` and `idea`); MCP
`CreateResultOut.duplicate_warning`. The message names the candidate's id/alias, its current
status, the age of its create, and states the create still succeeded (advisory, exit 0).
Every probe failure (unreadable journal, config error, reduce failure) degrades to
no-warning — an advisory must never fail a completed write.

**Portability.** The trigger is operation-linked and in-process (inside `create_core`, the
single seam every create funnels through: CLI, library, MCP, `idea()`); no CI dependency.
`fcntl` matches the existing HLC-sidecar precedent in-tree.

**Secondary AC (duplicates links for the two named tickets).** Phase-1 proved the sanctioned
post-close path works end-to-end: `reopen -> link <src> <target> duplicates -> transition
open closed --class duplicate` (the re-close is completion-verification-exempt via the
`_administrative_disposition` short-circuit). No code change; execute that runnable path on
`elfish-saltwater-pika` -> `woodblock-gnatty-xiaosaurus` (5a90-ec98) and
`decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` -> `039b-d179-b669-4439` so both carry machine-readable
`duplicates` links.

## File impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py` (new): journal read/prune/append + probe +
  `duplicate_create_warning`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`: call the probe in `create_core` beside
  `description_cap_warning`; CLI stderr emit in `create_cli`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/idea.py`: stderr emit of `duplicate_warning` in `idea_cli` (calls
  `create_core` directly, so it needs its own `_warn_stderr` call).
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`: log + carry `duplicate_warning` on `create_ticket`/`idea`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`: MCP result field.
- `src/rebar/types.py`, `src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json`: result shape.
- `docs/config.md`: note the create-time advisory under `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`.
- `tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py` (new).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Establish and record whether `rebar create` currently consults the overlap detector, with
      the file and line that does or does not. (Phase-1 answer: it does NOT — `create_core`,
      `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`, no `rebar.llm.overlap` import; record final line
      numbers in the close comment.)
- [x] A ticket whose title matches an existing ticket's is SURFACED at creation time — the author is
      told, with the candidate ticket's id and status. Proven by creating a same-title ticket in a
      test and asserting the signal appears. Title match is the minimum bar (normalized: case,
      punctuation, whitespace folded), bounded to the 600 s recency window per the measured design.
- [x] The signal does not block creation. Legitimate same-title tickets exist (follow-ups, retries,
      per-environment variants); the requirement is that the author is INFORMED, not prevented —
      exit code 0, ticket created, warning on stderr/logger/result-field only.
- [x] `rebar link <closed-source> <target> duplicates` is permitted, or a sanctioned alternative
      exists for recording a duplicate relation after the source is closed. Whichever is chosen,
      `elfish-saltwater-pika` and `decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` end up with machine-readable
      `duplicates` links rather than prose comments. (Sanctioned alternative proven by Phase-1:
      reopen -> link -> re-close `--class duplicate`; execute it on both tickets.)
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.

## Testing / Verification
- RED-first unit tests in `tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py` (modeled on
  `test_description_cap_warning.py`): same-title create within the window warns with the
  candidate's id and status on all surfaces (library dict, `create` and `idea` CLI stderr
  with pure stdout, MCP result field); distinct titles are silent; normalization folds
  case/punctuation/whitespace; an entry older than the window is silent; flag off = silent
  and no journal writes; a corrupt journal never fails the create; the warned create still
  succeeds (exit 0, ticket readable); two processes creating the same title concurrently
  serialize on the journal flock so at least one observes the other.
- Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py -q`,
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0 increased=0).
- Manual: in a scratch store with the flag on, create two same-title tickets seconds
  apart and observe the stderr advisory naming the first.
